newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia presidential election in September-official.
newsitem.headline: Serbia presidential election in September-official.

text.p: Presidential and parliamentary elections in Serbia will be held on September 21, the acting Serbian president and speaker of parliament, Dragan Tomic, said on Friday.
The office of Serbian president has been vacant since Wednesday when Slobodan Milosevic became president of Yugoslavia, which is made up of Serbia and Montenegro.
The dominant figure in Yugoslav politics since the breakup of the six-member federation in the early 1990s, Milosevic, 55, was prevented by the Serbian constitution from serving any further term.
Dragan Tomic took over the office and under the constitution was obliged to call an election within 60 days.
The candidate of Milosevic's ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) for the presidency has not yet been announced, but a senior SPS official has praised Zoran Lilic.

Lilic was the president of Yugoslavia until Milosevic took over the office. Diplomats said Lilic performed well in the mostly ceremonial post of federal president and has remained untarnished by scandal.
